To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genome of the LAB species Lactobacillus plantarum contains a wide variety of enzymes involved in the production of flavor compounds from amino acids.

1) Lactobacillus plantarum WCFS1 and L. plantarum ATCC 14917 encode a complete pathway for L-phenylalanine biosynthesis, and 2) L. plantaram strains WCFS1, ATCC 1491, and ATCC 1497 encode a complete pathway to produce 2,3-butanediol.
the comparative genomics of flavor enzymes in LAB can be used to predict the flavor profile of a strain, which is important for selecting the best starter culture for a particular dairy product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparative genomics of enzymes involved in amino acid metabolism and flavor formation in lactic acid bacteria.
the comparative genomics of enzymes in flavor forming pathways from amino acids in LAB.
the identification, characterization and application of enzymes from lactic acid bacteria that are involved in the formation of aroma and flavor compounds in dairy products.

the flavor of cheese is a result of a complex interaction between the milk, microbial and cheese manufacturing processes.
the use of LAB as starter cultures in fermented dairy products has a great influence on the flavor profile and that this influence is mainly due to the enzymes and the enzymes’ activity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LAB are capable of producing a large number of different compounds, and the metabolic routes for the formation of these compounds can vary greatly between strains.
we have identified a set of enzymes that are responsible for the production of a wide range of flavor compounds in lactic acid bacteria.
LAB have a great potential to produce various flavor compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the metabolic pathways of lactic acid bacteria are very diverse, and that the diversity of these bacteria is a result of a long history of adaptation to different environmental conditions and different food products.

the flavor compounds that contribute to the unique flavor of dairy products are not produced through a single metabolic pathway but rather through a variety of metabolic pathways, which are strain specific and are dependent on environmental factors.
we can use comparative genomics to understand the evolution of flavor-forming pathways in LAB.
